In Coding 7 you checked whether one sample was normal enough for a *t*-test. Today you run all three *t*-tests from lecture A009 on the same data the slides used: `chickwts` (71 chicks, six feeds) and `sleep` (ten patients, two sleeping drugs). Both are built into R, so there is nothing to download. The numbers you get should match the slides exactly.

The recipe is the same every time:

1.  Write H₀ and Hₐ as math.
2.  Choose the test and set α **before** you look.
3.  Look at the data, then check the assumptions.
4.  Compute the statistic and its p-value.
5.  p ≤ α: reject H₀. Otherwise: fail to reject. Never "accept".

The three tables below are a reference for this activity and for **Coding Assignment 4, Parts A and B**.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Which *t*-test? Read the design (click to expand)

| Design | Test | H₀ as math | Check normality on |
|---|---|---|---|
| One group vs. a number from outside the data | One-sample | μ = μ₀ | the group |
| Two **independent** groups | Welch two-sample | μ₁ = μ₂ | each group separately |
| The same unit measured twice, or matched pairs | Paired | μ_diff = 0 | the within-unit differences |

Welch's test does not assume equal variances, so you do not need a variance check before it. A paired *t*-test is a one-sample *t*-test on the differences, with `mu = 0`.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## `t.test()` arguments (click to expand)

| Argument | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `x` | A numeric vector (one sample, or the first of two) | `t.test(linseed_chicks$weight, mu = 200)` |
| `mu` | The hypothesized mean for a one-sample test | `mu = 200` |
| `alternative` | `"two.sided"` (default), `"greater"`, or `"less"` | `alternative = "greater"` |
| `y ~ group, data =` | Formula form: a continuous column split by a two-level column | `t.test(weight ~ feed, data = two_feeds)` |
| `x, y, paired = TRUE` | Two vectors of the same length, matched row by row | `t.test(drug2, drug1, paired = TRUE)` |

One-tailed tests put all of α in one tail. Name the direction **before** you see the data, and only when the other direction would change nothing you do.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Reading the output (click to expand)

Every test in this activity returns the same kind of object. Save it, print it, and pull pieces out with `$`.

| Piece | What it holds | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `$statistic` | The *t* value: signal ÷ noise | `t_one_sample$statistic` |
| `$parameter` | Degrees of freedom | `t_one_sample$parameter` |
| `$p.value` | Probability of a *t* this extreme if H₀ were true | `t_one_sample$p.value` |
| `$conf.int` | 95% confidence interval for the mean (or difference) | `t_one_sample$conf.int` |
| `$estimate` | The sample mean(s) or mean difference | `t_one_sample$estimate` |

`shapiro.test()` returns the same kind of object. Its H₀ is normality, so a small p-value is evidence **against** normality. A large one is not proof of normality.
:::

## Part A: One-sample *t*-test

**Research question:** Do linseed-fed chicks weigh more than 200 g on average?

H₀: μ = 200 g. Hₐ: μ > 200 g. One-sample *t*-test, one-tailed, α = 0.05. The direction is fixed now, before we look.

```{webr}
#| envir: ttests_lab
#| exercise: box_feed
#| check: true
had_error <- any(vapply(.evaluate_result, inherits, logical(1), "error"))
find_plot <- function(v, env) {
  if (inherits(v, "ggplot")) return(v)
  for (nm in rev(ls(env))) {
    o <- get(nm, envir = env)
    if (inherits(o, "ggplot")) return(o)
  }
  NULL
}
layer_class <- function(p, part) vapply(p$layers, function(l) class(l[[part]])[1], character(1))
p <- find_plot(.last_value, .envir_result)
if (had_error) {
  list(correct = FALSE, type = "info",
       message = "R stopped. Read the last line of the message. Layers are joined with `+`, and `aes()` sits inside `ggplot()`.")
} else if (is.null(p)) {
  list(correct = FALSE, type = "info",
       message = "No figure yet. Keep the `ggplot()` call and add `geom_boxplot()` with `+`.")
} else if (!"GeomBoxplot" %in% layer_class(p, "geom")) {
  list(correct = FALSE, type = "info",
       message = "A figure, but no boxes. Add `geom_boxplot()`.")
} else if (!exists("box_feed", envir = .envir_result, inherits = FALSE)) {
  list(correct = FALSE, type = "info",
       message = "Boxplot drawn. Save it as `box_feed` with `<-`.")
} else {
  list(correct = TRUE, type = "success",
       message = "Six boxes, one per feed. Now zoom in on linseed.")
}
```

```{webr}
#| envir: ttests_lab
#| exercise: linseed_chicks
#| check: true
had_error <- any(vapply(.evaluate_result, inherits, logical(1), "error"))
if (had_error) {

       message = "R stopped. Read the last line of the message. Is `linseed` in quotes, and is the comparison `==` with two equals signs?")
} else if (!exists("linseed_chicks", envir = .envir_result, inherits = FALSE)) {

       message = "Save the filtered table as `linseed_chicks` with `<-`.")

  if (!is.data.frame(lc)) {
    list(correct = FALSE, type = "info",

    list(correct = FALSE, type = "warning",
         message = "Zero rows. Check the spelling: the feed is `\"linseed\"`, all lowercase.")
  } else if (nrow(lc) == 12 && all(lc$feed == "linseed")) {
    list(correct = TRUE, type = "success",
         message = "12 linseed chicks. One group, ready for a one-sample test.")
  } else {
    list(correct = FALSE, type = "warning",
         message = paste0(nrow(lc), " rows. Only the 12 linseed chicks should remain."))
  }
}
```

### 6. Shapiro-Wilk on the linseed weights

Run `shapiro.test()` on `weight` in `linseed_chicks`. Save the result as `shapiro_linseed` and print it.

```{webr}
#| envir: ttests_lab
#| exercise: shapiro_linseed
shapiro_linseed <-

```

:::: {.hint exercise="shapiro_linseed"}
::: {.callout-note collapse="false"}
## Hint

Pass one numeric column with `$`.

``` r
shapiro.test(mtcars$mpg)
```
:::
::::

:::: {.solution exercise="shapiro_linseed"}
::: {.callout-tip collapse="false"}
## Solution

``` r
shapiro_linseed <- shapiro.test(linseed_chicks$weight)
shapiro_linseed
```

W = 0.969, p = 0.90. No evidence against normality. The same output is on the lecture slide.
:::
::::

```{webr}
#| envir: ttests_lab
#| exercise: shapiro_linseed
#| check: true
had_error <- any(vapply(.evaluate_result, inherits, logical(1), "error"))
if (had_error) {
  list(correct = FALSE, type = "info",
       message = "R stopped. Read the last line of the message. `shapiro.test()` needs one numeric vector, such as `linseed_chicks$weight`.")
} else if (!exists("shapiro_linseed", envir = .envir_result, inherits = FALSE)) {
  list(correct = FALSE, type = "info",
       message = "Save the result as `shapiro_linseed` with `<-`, then print it.")
} else {
  sl <- get("shapiro_linseed", envir = .envir_result)
  if (!inherits(sl, "htest") || is.null(sl$p.value)) {
    list(correct = FALSE, type = "info",
         message = "`shapiro_linseed` should be the output of `shapiro.test()`.")
  } else if (abs(sl$p.value - 0.9035) < 0.01) {
    list(correct = TRUE, type = "success",
         message = "p = 0.90. No evidence against normality; the one-sample t-test is appropriate.")
  } else {
    list(correct = FALSE, type = "warning",
         message = paste0("A Shapiro result, but p = ", signif(sl$p.value, 3), ". Test the 12 linseed weights; the slide shows p = 0.90."))
  }
}
```

### 7. One-tailed one-sample *t*-test

Test whether the mean linseed weight is **greater than** 200 g. Use `t.test()` with `mu = 200` and `alternative = "greater"`. Save the result as `t_one_sample` and print it.

```{webr}
#| envir: ttests_lab
#| exercise: t_one_sample
t_one_sample <-

```

:::: {.hint exercise="t_one_sample"}
::: {.callout-note collapse="false"}
## Hint

From `?t.test`: for one sample, pass a numeric vector, the hypothesized mean, and the direction.

``` r
t.test(mtcars$mpg, mu = 20, alternative = "greater")
```
:::
::::

:::: {.solution exercise="t_one_sample"}
::: {.callout-tip collapse="false"}
## Solution

``` r
t_one_sample <- t.test(linseed_chicks$weight, mu = 200, alternative = "greater")
t_one_sample
```

t = 1.24, df = 11, p = 0.12. Mean = 218.75 g; the one-sided 95% CI runs from 191.7 g upward and includes 200.
:::
::::

```{webr}
#| envir: ttests_lab
#| exercise: t_one_sample
#| check: true
had_error <- any(vapply(.evaluate_result, inherits, logical(1), "error"))
if (had_error) {
  list(correct = FALSE, type = "info",
       message = "R stopped. Read the last line of the message. Separate the arguments with commas: `t.test(x, mu = 200, alternative = \"greater\")`.")
} else if (!exists("t_one_sample", envir = .envir_result, inherits = FALSE)) {
  list(correct = FALSE, type = "info",
       message = "Save the result as `t_one_sample` with `<-`, then print it.")
} else {
  tt <- get("t_one_sample", envir = .envir_result)
  if (!inherits(tt, "htest") || is.null(tt$p.value)) {
    list(correct = FALSE, type = "info",
         message = "`t_one_sample` should be the output of `t.test()`.")
  } else if (!grepl("One Sample", tt$method)) {
    list(correct = FALSE, type = "warning",
         message = "That is not a one-sample test. Pass one vector (`linseed_chicks$weight`) and set `mu = 200`.")
  } else if (is.null(tt$null.value) || abs(tt$null.value - 200) > 1e-6) {
    list(correct = FALSE, type = "warning",
         message = "One-sample test, but the hypothesized mean is not 200. Set `mu = 200`.")
  } else if (tt$alternative != "greater") {
    list(correct = FALSE, type = "warning",
         message = paste0("Two-tailed p = ", signif(tt$p.value, 3), ". The question is directional: add `alternative = \"greater\"`."))
  } else if (abs(tt$p.value - 0.1198) < 0.005) {
    list(correct = TRUE, type = "success",
         message = "t = 1.24, df = 11, p = 0.12. Same numbers as the lecture slide.")
  } else {
    list(correct = FALSE, type = "warning",
         message = paste0("Right test, but p = ", signif(tt$p.value, 3), ". Test the 12 linseed weights only."))
  }
}
```

### 8. Make the call

Does the mean weight of linseed-fed chicks exceed 200 g at α = 0.05? Assign `linseed_above_200` to `TRUE` or `FALSE` (no quotes, all caps).

```{webr}
#| envir: ttests_lab
#| setup: true
#| exercise: linseed_above_200
library(tidyverse)
linseed_chicks <- chickwts |>
  filter(feed == "linseed")
t_one_sample <- t.test(linseed_chicks$weight, mu = 200, alternative = "greater")
```

```{webr}
#| envir: ttests_lab
#| exercise: linseed_above_200
linseed_above_200 <-
```

:::: {.hint exercise="linseed_above_200"}
::: {.callout-note collapse="false"}
## Hint

Compare `t_one_sample$p.value` with 0.05. The sample mean being above 200 is not enough on its own.
:::
::::

:::: {.solution exercise="linseed_above_200"}
::: {.callout-tip collapse="false"}
## Solution

``` r
linseed_above_200 <- FALSE
```

p = 0.12 is above α = 0.05, so we **fail to reject** H₀. The sample mean (218.75 g) is above 200, but a difference this size is easy to get by chance with 12 chicks. We do not "accept" that the mean is 200; we lack evidence that it is higher.
:::
::::

```{webr}
#| envir: ttests_lab
#| exercise: linseed_above_200
#| check: true
had_error <- any(vapply(.evaluate_result, inherits, logical(1), "error"))
if (had_error) {
  list(correct = FALSE, type = "info",
       message = "R stopped. `TRUE` and `FALSE` are written in all caps with no quotes.")
} else if (!exists("linseed_above_200", envir = .envir_result, inherits = FALSE)) {
  list(correct = FALSE, type = "info",
       message = "Assign `linseed_above_200 <- TRUE` or `FALSE`.")
} else {
  ans <- get("linseed_above_200", envir = .envir_result)
  if (!is.logical(ans) || length(ans) != 1 || is.na(ans)) {
    list(correct = FALSE, type = "info",
         message = "`linseed_above_200` should be exactly `TRUE` or `FALSE`.")
  } else if (isTRUE(ans)) {
    list(correct = FALSE, type = "warning",
         message = "p = 0.12 is above 0.05. A sample mean above 200 is not the same as evidence that the population mean is above 200.")
  } else {
    list(correct = TRUE, type = "success",
         message = "FALSE. Fail to reject H0: no evidence that linseed chicks average more than 200 g.")
  }
}
```

## Part B: Welch two-sample *t*-test

**Research question:** Do linseed and meatmeal chicks differ in mean weight?

H₀: μ_linseed = μ_meatmeal. Hₐ: μ_linseed ≠ μ_meatmeal. Welch two-sample *t*-test, two-tailed, α = 0.05. Different chicks ate each feed, so the groups are independent.

### 9. Keep two feeds

Filter `chickwts` to the linseed and meatmeal rows. Save the result as `two_feeds`.

```{webr}
#| envir: ttests_lab
#| setup: true
#| exercise: two_feeds
library(tidyverse)
```

```{webr}

shapiro_linseed <-

```

::: {.callout-note collapse="false"}
## Hint

Two routes to one group's weights. Pick either.

``` r
# square brackets: keep the mpg values where cyl is 4
shapiro.test(mtcars$mpg[mtcars$cyl == 4])

# filter then pull
cyl4 <- mtcars |> filter(cyl == 4) |> pull(mpg)
shapiro.test(cyl4)
```
:::
::::

:::: {.solution exercise="shapiro_two_feeds"}
::: {.callout-tip collapse="false"}
## Solution

``` r
shapiro_linseed <- shapiro.test(two_feeds$weight[two_feeds$feed == "linseed"])
shapiro_meatmeal <- shapiro.test(two_feeds$weight[two_feeds$feed == "meatmeal"])
shapiro_linseed
shapiro_meatmeal
```

Linseed p = 0.90, meatmeal p = 0.96. No evidence against normality in either group.
:::
::::

```{webr}
#| envir: ttests_lab
#| exercise: shapiro_two_feeds
#| check: true
had_error <- any(vapply(.evaluate_result, inherits, logical(1), "error"))
if (had_error) {
  list(correct = FALSE, type = "info",
       message = "R stopped. Read the last line of the message. Inside square brackets the condition needs the full column name: `two_feeds$feed == \"linseed\"`.")
} else if (!exists("shapiro_linseed", envir = .envir_result, inherits = FALSE) ||
           !exists("shapiro_meatmeal", envir = .envir_result, inherits = FALSE)) {
  list(correct = FALSE, type = "info",
       message = "Save both results, as `shapiro_linseed` and `shapiro_meatmeal`.")
} else {
  sl <- get("shapiro_linseed", envir = .envir_result)
  sm <- get("shapiro_meatmeal", envir = .envir_result)
  if (!inherits(sl, "htest") || !inherits(sm, "htest")) {
    list(correct = FALSE, type = "info",
         message = "Both objects should be the output of `shapiro.test()`.")
  } else if (abs(sl$p.value - sm$p.value) < 1e-8) {
    list(correct = FALSE, type = "warning",
         message = "Both tests gave the same p-value, so they ran on the same vector. Subset to each feed separately.")
  } else if (abs(sl$p.value - 0.9035) < 0.01 && abs(sm$p.value - 0.9612) < 0.01) {
    list(correct = TRUE, type = "success",
         message = "Linseed p = 0.90, meatmeal p = 0.96. Each group passes on its own.")
  } else {
    list(correct = FALSE, type = "warning",
         message = paste0("Two Shapiro results, but p = ", signif(sl$p.value, 3), " and ", signif(sm$p.value, 3), ". Each test should see only one feed's 11 or 12 weights."))
  }
}
```

### 12. Welch two-sample *t*-test

Run a Welch two-sample *t*-test of `weight` by `feed` in `two_feeds`. Save it as `t_two_sample` and print it.

```{webr}
#| envir: ttests_lab
#| exercise: t_two_sample
t_two_sample <-

```

:::: {.hint exercise="t_two_sample"}
::: {.callout-note collapse="false"}
## Hint

Formula form: the continuous column, a tilde, the grouping column, then `data =`. Welch is the default.

``` r
t.test(mpg ~ am, data = mtcars)
```

Coding Assignment 4 uses this form. The lecture slide passed two vectors instead: `t.test(weights_meatmeal, weights_linseed)`. Same test, same p-value, sign of *t* flipped.
:::
::::

:::: {.solution exercise="t_two_sample"}
::: {.callout-tip collapse="false"}
## Solution

``` r
t_two_sample <- t.test(weight ~ feed, data = two_feeds)
t_two_sample
```

t = −2.35, df = 19.2, p = 0.029. The difference (linseed − meatmeal) is −58 g, 95% CI −109.8 to −6.5 g. The lecture's *t* is +2.35 because it subtracted in the other order.
:::
::::

```{webr}
#| envir: ttests_lab
#| exercise: t_two_sample
#| check: true
had_error <- any(vapply(.evaluate_result, inherits, logical(1), "error"))
if (had_error) {
  list(correct = FALSE, type = "info",
       message = "R stopped. Read the last line of the message. The formula is `weight ~ feed`, and the table goes in `data = two_feeds`.")
} else if (!exists("t_two_sample", envir = .envir_result, inherits = FALSE)) {
  list(correct = FALSE, type = "info",
       message = "Save the result as `t_two_sample` with `<-`, then print it.")
} else {
  tt <- get("t_two_sample", envir = .envir_result)
  if (!inherits(tt, "htest") || is.null(tt$p.value)) {
    list(correct = FALSE, type = "info",
         message = "`t_two_sample` should be the output of `t.test()`.")
  } else if (grepl("Paired", tt$method)) {
    list(correct = FALSE, type = "warning",
         message = "That is a paired test. Different chicks ate each feed, so the groups are independent: drop `paired = TRUE`.")
  } else if (!grepl("Welch", tt$method)) {
    list(correct = FALSE, type = "warning",
         message = "Not a Welch test. Remove `var.equal = TRUE`; Welch is the default.")
  } else if (tt$alternative != "two.sided") {
    list(correct = FALSE, type = "warning",
         message = "One-tailed. The question is whether the feeds differ, in either direction, so use the two-sided default.")
  } else if (abs(tt$p.value - 0.02933) < 0.002) {
    list(correct = TRUE, type = "success",
         message = paste0("Welch t = ", round(unname(tt$statistic), 2), ", df = 19.2, p = 0.029. Same numbers as the slide."))
  } else {
    list(correct = FALSE, type = "warning",
         message = paste0("Welch test, but p = ", signif(tt$p.value, 3), ". Use `data = two_feeds` so only linseed and meatmeal are compared."))
  }
}
```

## Part C: Paired *t*-test

**Research question:** Do two sleeping drugs differ in the extra sleep they give?

The `sleep` data record extra hours of sleep for ten patients, each of whom tried drug 1 and drug 2. The same person measured twice is a **paired** design. H₀: μ_diff = 0. Hₐ: μ_diff ≠ 0, where diff = drug 2 − drug 1 within each patient. Paired *t*-test, two-tailed, α = 0.05.

**Answers:** 10 patients, each appearing twice; `group` is the drug (1 or 2) and `ID` is the patient; every patient tried both drugs, so each drug-2 value has a matching drug-1 value from the same person.

```{webr}
layer_class <- function(p, part) vapply(p$layers, function(l) class(l[[part]])[1], character(1))
p <- find_plot(.last_value, .envir_result)
if (had_error) {
  list(correct = FALSE, type = "info",
       message = "R stopped. Read the last line of the message. Layers are joined with `+`.")
} else if (is.null(p)) {
  list(correct = FALSE, type = "info",
       message = "No figure yet. Keep the `ggplot()` call and add `geom_histogram()` with `+`.")
} else if (!"StatBin" %in% layer_class(p, "stat")) {
  list(correct = FALSE, type = "info",
       message = "A figure, but not a histogram. Add `geom_histogram()`.")
} else if (!exists("hist_delta", envir = .envir_result, inherits = FALSE)) {
  list(correct = FALSE, type = "info",
       message = "Histogram drawn. Save it as `hist_delta` with `<-`.")
} else {
  list(correct = TRUE, type = "success",
       message = "Histogram of the ten differences. Note the one value near 4.6.")
}
```

### 19. Shapiro-Wilk on the differences

For a paired design you check the **differences**, not drug 1 and drug 2 separately. Run `shapiro.test()` on `sleep_delta`. Save it as `shapiro_delta` and print it.

```{webr}
#| envir: ttests_lab
#| exercise: shapiro_delta
shapiro_delta <-

```

:::: {.hint exercise="shapiro_delta"}
::: {.callout-note collapse="false"}
## Hint

Same function as step 6, applied to `sleep_wide$sleep_delta`.
:::
::::

:::: {.solution exercise="shapiro_delta"}
::: {.callout-tip collapse="false"}
## Solution

``` r
shapiro_delta <- shapiro.test(sleep_wide$sleep_delta)
shapiro_delta
```

W = 0.83, p = 0.033. The differences fail the normality check, because of patient 9.
:::
::::

```{webr}
#| envir: ttests_lab
#| exercise: shapiro_delta
#| check: true
had_error <- any(vapply(.evaluate_result, inherits, logical(1), "error"))
if (had_error) {
  list(correct = FALSE, type = "info",
       message = "R stopped. Read the last line of the message. Pass one column: `sleep_wide$sleep_delta`.")
} else if (!exists("shapiro_delta", envir = .envir_result, inherits = FALSE)) {
  list(correct = FALSE, type = "info",
       message = "Save the result as `shapiro_delta` with `<-`, then print it.")
} else {
  sd_ <- get("shapiro_delta", envir = .envir_result)
  if (!inherits(sd_, "htest") || is.null(sd_$p.value)) {
    list(correct = FALSE, type = "info",
         message = "`shapiro_delta` should be the output of `shapiro.test()`.")
  } else if (abs(sd_$p.value - 0.03334) < 0.005) {
    list(correct = TRUE, type = "success",
         message = "p = 0.033. The differences fail the check. Read the callout below before you decide what to do.")
  } else {
    list(correct = FALSE, type = "warning",
         message = paste0("A Shapiro result, but p = ", signif(sd_$p.value, 3), ". Test the ten differences, not the drug 1 or drug 2 values."))
  }
}
```

::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
## One odd patient, n = 10: what to do

The check failed because one patient gained 4.6 hours. Work through the questions from Coding 7.

-   **Impossible?** No. **Data-entry error?** No reason to think so. Keep the point.
-   **Transform?** Adding a constant to the differences changes H₀ from "mean difference = 0" to something with no biological meaning. The "+ c" trick is for skewed positive data with zeros, not for paired differences.
-   **Small n.** With ten values the normality test is weak, and one value can tip it.

So: run the paired *t*-test, report the failed check honestly, and run a **sensitivity check** without patient 9. If the conclusion is the same either way, say so.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Check yourself

The differences fail the normality check because one patient gained 4.6 hours. What should you do?

A.  Remove patient 9 and rerun the check\
B.  Run the paired *t*-test and report the caveat\
C.  Switch to a two-sample *t*-test

**Answer:** B. Deleting a real, possible value to pass a check is not analysis. Switching to a two-sample test throws away the pairing, which is the whole point of the design.
:::

### 20. Paired *t*-test

Run a paired *t*-test on `drug2` and `drug1` in `sleep_wide`, drug 2 first. Save it as `t_paired` and print it.

```{webr}
#| envir: ttests_lab
#| exercise: t_paired
t_paired <-
```

:::: {.hint exercise="t_paired"}

## Hint

Two vectors of the same length and `paired = TRUE`. The first vector minus the second is the difference being tested.

``` r
after <- c(11, 13, 12)
before <- c(10, 12, 11)
t.test(after, before, paired = TRUE)
```
:::
::::

:::: {.solution exercise="t_paired"}
::: {.callout-tip collapse="false"}
## Solution

``` r
t_paired <- t.test(sleep_wide$drug2, sleep_wide$drug1, paired = TRUE)
t_paired
```

t = 4.06, df = 9, p = 0.0028. Mean difference 1.58 hours, 95% CI 0.70 to 2.46 hours. Same as the slide.
:::
::::

```{webr}
#| envir: ttests_lab
#| exercise: t_paired
#| check: true
had_error <- any(vapply(.evaluate_result, inherits, logical(1), "error"))
if (had_error) {
  list(correct = FALSE, type = "info",
       message = "R stopped. Read the last line of the message. Pass two columns with `$`, separated by a comma, then `paired = TRUE`.")
} else if (!exists("t_paired", envir = .envir_result, inherits = FALSE)) {
  list(correct = FALSE, type = "info",
       message = "Save the result as `t_paired` with `<-`, then print it.")
} else {
  tp <- get("t_paired", envir = .envir_result)
  if (!inherits(tp, "htest") || is.null(tp$p.value)) {
    list(correct = FALSE, type = "info",
         message = "`t_paired` should be the output of `t.test()`.")
  } else if (!grepl("Paired", tp$method)) {
    list(correct = FALSE, type = "warning",
         message = paste0("Not a paired test (p = ", signif(tp$p.value, 3), "). The same ten patients tried both drugs, so add `paired = TRUE`."))
  } else if (abs(tp$p.value - 0.002833) > 0.001) {
    list(correct = FALSE, type = "warning",
         message = paste0("Paired test, but p = ", signif(tp$p.value, 3), ". Use the `drug2` and `drug1` columns of `sleep_wide`."))
  } else if (unname(tp$estimate) < 0) {
    list(correct = TRUE, type = "info",
         message = "Correct test and p-value, but the difference is drug 1 − drug 2 (−1.58). Put `drug2` first so the sign matches the hypothesis.")
  } else {
    list(correct = TRUE, type = "success",
         message = "t = 4.06, df = 9, p = 0.0028. Mean difference 1.58 hours in favor of drug 2.")
  }
}
```

### 21. Same test, two ways

A paired *t*-test is a one-sample *t*-test on the differences with `mu = 0`. Run the block and compare the two *t* statistics and p-values.

```{webr}
#| envir: ttests_lab
#| setup: true
#| exercise: paired_two_ways
library(tidyverse)
sleep_wide <- sleep |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = extra, names_prefix = "drug") |>
  mutate(sleep_delta = drug2 - drug1)
```

```{webr}
#| envir: ttests_lab
#| exercise: paired_two_ways
t_from_columns <- t.test(sleep_wide$drug2, sleep_wide$drug1, paired = TRUE)
t_from_delta <- t.test(sleep_wide$sleep_delta, mu = 0)
t_from_columns$statistic
t_from_delta$statistic
t_from_columns$p.value
t_from_delta$p.value
```

:::: {.hint exercise="paired_two_ways"}
::: {.callout-note collapse="false"}
## Hint

Run the block as written. The only difference between the two calls is who does the subtraction: R, or you in step 17.
:::
::::

:::: {.solution exercise="paired_two_ways"}
::: {.callout-tip collapse="false"}
## Solution

Both give t = 4.06 and p = 0.0028. That is why the normality check goes on the differences: they are the one sample the test actually sees.
:::
::::

```{webr}
#| envir: ttests_lab
#| exercise: paired_two_ways
#| check: true
had_error <- any(vapply(.evaluate_result, inherits, logical(1), "error"))
if (had_error) {
  list(correct = FALSE, type = "info",
       message = "R stopped. Read the last line of the message, then restore the block as written.")
} else if (!exists("t_from_columns", envir = .envir_result, inherits = FALSE) ||
           !exists("t_from_delta", envir = .envir_result, inherits = FALSE)) {
  list(correct = FALSE, type = "info",
       message = "Run the block so both `t_from_columns` and `t_from_delta` exist.")
} else {
  a <- get("t_from_columns", envir = .envir_result)
  b <- get("t_from_delta", envir = .envir_result)
  if (inherits(a, "htest") && inherits(b, "htest") && abs(a$p.value - b$p.value) < 1e-10) {
    list(correct = TRUE, type = "success",
         message = "Identical t and p. A paired test is a one-sample test on the differences.")
  } else {
    list(correct = FALSE, type = "info",
         message = "The two p-values should match exactly. Restore the block as written.")
  }
}
```

### 22. Sensitivity check

Rerun the one-sample test on the differences **without patient 9** and see whether the conclusion changes. The block is written for you.

```{webr}
#| envir: ttests_lab
#| exercise: sensitivity
without_9 <- sleep_wide |>
  filter(ID != "9")
t.test(without_9$sleep_delta, mu = 0)
```

:::: {.hint exercise="sensitivity"}
::: {.callout-note collapse="false"}
## Hint

`ID` is a factor, so the patient number goes in quotes. Nine differences remain.
:::
::::

:::: {.solution exercise="sensitivity"}
::: {.callout-tip collapse="false"}
## Solution

With all ten patients, p = 0.0028. Without patient 9, t = 5.66, df = 8, p = 0.0005. Same conclusion either way, so the failed normality check does not change the answer. Report the test on all ten and say that.
:::
::::

```{webr}
#| envir: ttests_lab
#| exercise: sensitivity
#| check: true
had_error <- any(vapply(.evaluate_result, inherits, logical(1), "error"))
v <- .last_value
if (had_error) {
  list(correct = FALSE, type = "info",
       message = "R stopped. Read the last line of the message, then restore the block as written.")
} else if (inherits(v, "htest") && !is.null(v$parameter) && abs(unname(v$parameter) - 8) < 1e-6) {
  list(correct = TRUE, type = "success",
       message = "df = 8, p = 0.0005 without patient 9. Same conclusion as with all ten.")
} else {
  list(correct = FALSE, type = "info",
       message = "The last line should print a one-sample t-test on nine differences (df = 8).")
}
```

## 24. Recap: functions you practiced

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## What does each function do?

| Function | Role |
|---|---|
| `glimpse()` | Rows, columns, and types |
| `filter()` with `==` or `%in%` | Keep one group, or two |
| `ggplot()` + `geom_boxplot()` | Compare a continuous variable across groups |
| `ggplot()` + `geom_histogram()` + `facet_wrap()` | Shape of each group, one panel each |
| `ggplot()` + `geom_line()` with `group = ID` | Spaghetti plot: each pair joined by a line |
| `pivot_wider()` | One row per patient, one column per drug |
| `mutate()` | Compute the within-patient difference |
| `shapiro.test()` | Normality check (H₀: data are normal) |
| `t.test(x, mu = ..., alternative = "greater")` | One-sample, one-tailed |
| `t.test(y ~ group, data = ...)` | Welch two-sample, two-tailed by default |
| `t.test(x, y, paired = TRUE)` | Paired |
| `t.test(delta, mu = 0)` | The same paired test, done by hand |
| `$p.value`, `$estimate`, `$conf.int` | Pull one piece out of a test result |

If you can explain each row in your own words, you have covered **Coding Assignment 4, Parts A and B**.
:::

::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
## Three things to say in your write-up

1.  **"Fail to reject" is not "accept".** The linseed test gave p = 0.12. That is not evidence that the mean is 200 g; it is a lack of evidence that it is higher. Twelve chicks is a small sample.
2.  **Report the effect, not just the p-value.** Meatmeal chicks were heavier by 58 g (95% CI 6.5 to 109.8 g). Drug 2 added 1.58 hours of sleep (95% CI 0.70 to 2.46). The interval tells the reader how big and how certain.
3.  **Report failed checks and what you did about them.** The sleep differences failed Shapiro-Wilk (p = 0.033) because of one patient. The sensitivity check without that patient gave the same conclusion. Say both.
:::

## Keep playing

**Wrong test, wrong answer.** What if you forgot the pairing and ran a two-sample test on the sleep data?

```{webr}
#| envir: ttests_lab
library(tidyverse)
t.test(extra ~ group, data = sleep)
```

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
p = 0.079. Not significant. The paired test on the same twenty numbers gave p = 0.0028. Patients differ from each other by hours, and the two-sample test treats all of that as noise. Pairing removes it. The test you choose follows from how the data were collected.
:::

**Two tails instead of one.** Rerun the linseed test without `alternative = "greater"`.

```{webr}
#| envir: ttests_lab
library(tidyverse)
linseed_chicks <- chickwts |> filter(feed == "linseed")
t.test(linseed_chicks$weight, mu = 200)
```

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
p = 0.24, twice the one-tailed 0.12. A one-tailed test is a choice you make before looking. If a two-tailed test gives p = 0.08 and you switch to one-tailed afterward to get p = 0.04, that is not a result. It is a decision made after the data.
:::

**Which test?** For each design, say which *t*-test you would run and what you would check for normality.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Check yourself

1.  Blood glucose measured in 20 rats, then again in the same 20 rats two hours after a glucose dose.
2.  Mean height of every BILD 5 student compared with a random sample of 300 UCSD students.
3.  Is the lead level in one well above the legal limit? Ten samples from that well.

**Answers:** (1) paired; check the 20 within-rat differences. (2) Welch two-sample; check each group separately. (3) one-sample, one-tailed, `alternative = "greater"`; check the ten samples. The direction is justified because a level *below* the limit changes nothing you do.
:::
